subject: Genetics
title: Mental Health and Methylation
description: A quick, practical guide to Mental Health and Methylation.

hook.text: Suicide victims' brains show different methylation patterns on stress-response genes.

buildup.text: The glucocorticoid receptor gene NR3C1 is more methylated in brains of people who experienced childhood abuse and later.

discovery.text: Higher methylation means fewer stress receptors. The brain can't regulate cortisol properly.

twist.text: Antidepressants may work partly through epigenetic mechanisms.

climax.text: Epigenetics offers hope: if depression involves reversible marks, treatments could target those marks directly—not just.

punchline.text: Trauma marks the brain. Epigenetic therapy may erase it.

quiz.question: What epigenetic change was found in suicide victims' brains?
